match.reason: The closest bank point only covers the basic graphs of sin x and cos x with amplitude 1 and tangent, so it does not teach the general a, n and k transformations this point needs, which is a change of depth rather than a small adjustment.

draft.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
card: The graphs of y = a sin(nx) + k and y = a cos(nx) + k are smooth waves that repeat. Here a, n and k are numbers, and a and n are positive.
Amplitude
The amplitude is a. It is the distance from the middle line up to a peak. The wave goes from k − a to k + a.
Period
The period is 2π ÷ n. It is the length of one full wave along the x-axis. A larger n gives a shorter period.
Mean value
The mean value is k. It is the height of the middle line. Example: y = 3 sin(2x) + 1 has amplitude 3, period 2π ÷ 2 = π, mean 1, and goes from −2 to 4.
draft.remember: a is the height of the wave, 2π ÷ n is its length, and k is its middle.

a.q: What is the period of y = 2 cos(4x) + 5?
a.why: Period = 2π ÷ n = 2π ÷ 4 = π/2. The tempting answer 2π is the period of y = cos x, which only applies when n = 1.
a.clue: Divide 2π by the number multiplying x.

b.q: What are the greatest and least values of y = 4 sin(3x) − 2?
b.why: The mean is −2 and the amplitude is 4, so y goes from −2 − 4 = −6 up to −2 + 4 = 2. The option 4 and −4 forgets to shift the wave by k.
b.clue: Start at the middle line, then go up and down by the amplitude.

problems.detail: "a is the height of the wave" is ambiguous. A student could read it as the full peak-to-trough height (2a), but the card defines a as the distance from the middle line up to a peak. Something like "a is the distance from the middle to a peak" would match the card.

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with a single right answer each (π/2; 2 and −6). The only problem is that the remember line calls a "the height of the wave", which could be misread as peak-to-trough height and does not match the card's definition of amplitude.

final.title: Graphs of sine and cosine
card: The graphs of \(y = a \sin(nx) + k\) and \(y = a \cos(nx) + k\) are smooth waves that repeat. Here \(a\), \(n\) and \(k\) are numbers, and \(a\) and \(n\) are positive.
Amplitude
The amplitude is \(a\). It is the distance from the middle line up to a peak. The wave goes from \(k - a\) to \(k + a\).
Period
The period is \(2\pi \div n\). It is the length of one full wave along the x-axis. A larger \(n\) gives a shorter period.
Mean value
The mean value is \(k\). It is the height of the middle line. Example: \(y = 3 \sin(2x) + 1\) has amplitude 3, period \(2\pi \div 2 = \pi\), mean 1, and goes from \(-2\) to 4.
final.remember: \(a\) is the distance from the middle to a peak, \(2\pi \div n\) is the length of one wave, and \(k\) is the height of the middle line.

a.why: Period \(= 2\pi \div n = 2\pi \div 4 = \frac{\pi}{2}\). The tempting answer \(2\pi\) is the period of \(y = \cos x\), which applies when \(n = 1\).

b.q: What are the greatest and least values of \(y = 4 \sin(3x) - 2\)?
b.why: The mean is \(-2\) and the amplitude is 4, so \(y\) goes from \(-2 - 4 = -6\) up to \(-2 + 4 = 2\). The option 4 and \(-4\) forgets to shift the wave by \(k\).
b.clue: Start at the middle line, then go up and down by the amplitude.
